criteria.criterion: A unit test in verify.rs shows judge() passes when a check failed in the baseline and fails again at verification, with the failure recorded as pre-existing and not listed in the verdict's failure reasons. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: verify::tests::a_check_failing_on_the_base_and_again_is_pre_existing_and_does_not_fail_the_verdict passed (17 of 17 verify tests ok). It asserts the note starts with PRE_EXISTING_NOTE, final_verdict is Pass and reasons are empty. It also checks that marking twice is a no-op and that judge alone gives Pass.

criteria.criterion: A unit test shows a check that passed in the baseline (or has no baseline entry) and fails at verification still makes the final verdict fail, with a reason naming it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
criteria.evidence: a_check_that_passed_or_was_absent_at_the_base_still_fails_the_verdict passed. It covers three cases: the check passed on the base, the baseline only has another check, and there is no baseline. Each asserts Fail, the reason 'check test failed', and no note.

criteria.criterion: A lifecycle test shows that when one check fails, the verifier still runs and every acceptance criterion in the verification record has its own result, while the final verdict still fails on that check. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
criteria.evidence: a_failing_check_still_runs_the_verifier_and_every_criterion_is_judged passed (50 of 50 lifecycle tests ok). It asserts the Verifier role was called, verification.json has 2 criteria and none says 'did not assess', final_verdict is Fail, the state is Rejected, and each failed check is named in the reasons without the pre-existing note.

criteria.criterion: A lifecycle test shows a job whose base commit already fails a check, and whose change leaves it failing, can pass verification when everything else passes. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
criteria.evidence: a_check_already_failing_on_the_base_does_not_reject_a_job_that_leaves_it_failing passed. The `old` check (sh -c 'exit 1') fails in the baseline and at verification; the job is Landed with a Pass verdict, empty reasons and the pre-existing note. In the counter case (`new` passes on the base and fails after the change) the job is Rejected.

criteria.criterion: The verification record marks pre-existing failures distinctly (for example in the check note), so a reader sees which failures were already on the base.
criteria.evidence: From reading the change: records.rs adds PRE_EXISTING_NOTE ('pre-existing: this check already failed on the base commit'), and verify.rs mark_pre_existing puts it at the start of the check note. run.rs calls it on check_runs before the checks are stored in the Verification record. introspect.rs failure_details leaves these checks out of the listed causes, and a new unit test covers that.

criteria.criterion: A missing baseline, or one with a note saying it could not run, treats no failure as pre-existing. An empty baseline is never read as success.
criteria.evidence: From reading the change: Baseline::failed_before needs note.is_none() and a failed entry with the same name, and run.rs drops a baseline whose base_commit differs from this job's base. Tests cover these cases: an_empty_or_noted_baseline_excuses_nothing (verify.rs, passed), only_a_noteless_baseline_with_a_failed_entry_excuses_a_check (records.rs, passed in the full cargo test run), and the None case in the criterion 2 test.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass with no new warnings.
criteria.evidence: In this snapshot, every test binary in `cargo test -q` reported ok with 0 failed. I re-ran it with -q because the plain `cargo test` output was saved outside the working directory, where policy does not let me read it. Clippy finished with no warnings, and fmt --check printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md records the new behavior in plain language for an outside reader.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: under Added, a new entry says checks that fail on the base are marked pre-existing and no longer reject the job, and that a missing, empty or could-not-run baseline excuses nothing. Under Fixed, a new entry says the verifier now still runs, so every criterion is judged.

findings.summary: The edited module doc line in verify.rs is much longer than the lines around it.
findings.evidence: The '//! finding is a blocker or major, and every check passed or was already failing on the base commit. Each `behavior` criterion must cite at least one' line was not rewrapped. rustfmt does not wrap comments, so fmt --check still passes.

findings.summary: There is an extra blank line between the new Fixed entry and the next one in CHANGELOG.md.
findings.evidence: The diff adds an entry under '### Fixed' and then a blank line before the existing 'Job planning no longer crashes' bullet. The other entries in the list have no blank lines between them.

summary: The change does what was asked. If a check failed on the job's base commit, and fails again on the candidate under the same name, the verification record marks it pre-existing by putting a fixed phrase at the start of its note. That check no longer fails the verdict. The verifier now runs even when a check fails, so every acceptance criterion gets its own result, and the final verdict still fails on any failure that is not pre-existing. Pre-existing marking happens only with a baseline that has no note and a failed entry of the same name, taken on this job's base commit. A missing, empty or could-not-run baseline excuses nothing. I ran the targeted verify and lifecycle tests, the full `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` in this snapshot, and all passed. All six changed files are on the expected list. I found two small formatting nits and nothing serious.
